requirements.requirement: Require new user passwords on node1 to be at least 12 characters long
requirements.summary: minlen=12 was set in /etc/security/pwquality.conf, confirmed present before and after reboot, and directly validated by rejecting an 8-character password and accepting a 12+ character password.

requirements.requirement: Require new user passwords on node1 to use at least three different character classes
requirements.summary: minclass=3 was set in /etc/security/pwquality.conf, confirmed present before and after reboot, and directly validated by rejecting a 12+ character password with only 2 character classes (lowercase-only) and accepting a 12+ character, 3-class password.

requirements.requirement: Policy is actually enforced when a regular (non-root) user changes their own password
requirements.summary: cmd-efc8ff6c96904ff6 shows a non-root user's password change attempt failing for a short password (exit 1), failing for a 2-class 12+ char password (exit 1), and succeeding for a compliant 12+ char/3-class password (exit 0). This was re-verified with a fresh test user post-reboot in cmd-b7af070de3d74806 with identical results.

requirements.requirement: Independent provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id and healthy config/enforcement state captured (cmd-707d848724b34b1f), reboot triggered and acknowledged (cmd-70cd11ef32574281), node observed unreachable during the transition (cmd-420d1eb61a4b49cb, cmd-308cabe21fdd42f5), then reachable again with a changed boot_id (cmd-8bb773af77fb4dc9, confirmed also by global:after_executor:node1:boot-identity vs global:before_prepare:node1:boot-identity), and post-restart recovery of config and live enforcement behavior directly re-tested (cmd-b7af070de3d74806).

overall_summary: The executor correctly set minlen=12 and minclass=3 in /etc/security/pwquality.conf on node1 and directly demonstrated enforcement for a non-root user's password changes (short password rejected, 2-class password rejected, compliant 12+/3-class password accepted), both before and after a full reboot. The mandatory provider-wide restart protocol was completed with a clean pre-restart baseline, an observed unreachable window, a changed boot_id, and re-verified post-restart configuration and enforcement behavior. The only shortfall is minor: several diagnostic log files written to /tmp during password-testing steps were left behind rather than cleaned up, though they pose negligible risk.
limitations: Only stdout/exit codes for passwd commands were captured; raw log file contents (/tmp/*.log) were not independently inspected beyond what was echoed in command output.
The full pwquality.conf file contents were not shown, only the minlen/minclass grep lines, so other directives in the file (if any pre-existed) cannot be fully assessed.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands were tied to the task: backing up and editing pwquality.conf (cmd-e3c524ca0fec4b56) was the core mutation and is retained as intended; creating and removing three test users (pwpolicytest, pwpolicytest2, pwpolicytest3) across cmd-e3c524ca0fec4b56, cmd-efc8ff6c96904ff6, cmd-b7af070de3d74806 was bounded, low-risk, and fully reverted via userdel each time. However, the diagnostic redirection files these commands wrote to /tmp (/tmp/short.log, /tmp/twoclass.log, /tmp/good.log, /tmp/init.log, /tmp/init3.log, /tmp/nonroot_short.log, /tmp/nonroot_twoclass.log, /tmp/nonroot_good.log, /tmp/p3_short.log, /tmp/p3_two.log, /tmp/p3_good.log, /tmp/reboot.log) were never cleaned up and are visible as residue in the after-executor temporary-files snapshot. This is low-risk (contains only passwd prompt text, not echoed secrets) but is unnecessary retained residue from otherwise-legitimate verification steps.
